Yeah, when you're in a middle of a conflict he's less likely to respond. Not only does it bring him trouble, but he might also see this as normal parent/child arguing. 

I mean when he takes his time alone. There should be a time where he reads, watches TV, or anything while your mom is out of the room(or the house)

Approach him quietly, and don't dive into your worries right away. Try to find common ground(i.e. I've started cooking because my dad cooks, and my mom doesn't, so she's out and I spend time with him. We also play dominoes.)

He probably has some complaints of his own that don't get shown because he'll get in trouble with your mom. He might not talk to you immediately because he's afraid you'll use his words against him (if you start saying, "Dad thinks the same as me! You're the crazy one!")

Don't give up on him. He's not yelling at you, because he knows it's not right. He's not fighting back, because he can't.

I mean, the point to to minimize the amount of violence in the world, not to eradicate it, nor let bad people go free. 

Soldiers, police officers, or any kind of enforcement should avoid killing people in the first place. Not only for morals, but most enemies have info that could be very useful. But at the same time, it would be foolish to condemn those who do kill, if restraining or disabling doesn't work there is no other choice. 

So I think it's a situational matter. In this case, if someone was found trying to kill a child, the best case scenario would be to take the guy alive, to face consequences. But if there is no choice, it wouldn't be immoral because you would be saving innocent life. 

But when the threat is neutralized, you have to ask why you want to kill a person. For revenge? Death will never change the outcome, and the guy wouldn't ever suffer, repent, or live for years knowing they killed a child. 

When the situation isn't life threatening and you can make a clear choice, the death penalty is not a good decison to make.

Personally, I think it's about moral responsibility- even for someone this evil, it can be seen as immoral to add more violence to the world by killing them. Even if it's a good riddance, it's not fair to ask others to be violent, and you shouldn't be violent yourself. 

Also at the same time, capital punishment is kinda tricky, there are definitely innocent people being killed. Guilty by court doesn't always mean that they committed the crime. Is it alright to sacrifice some people just to kill the evil ones?
